flagged.evidence: The cited dependency thm-injective-modules-over-a-pid-are-exactly-divisible begins: “Assume the Axiom of Choice through Baer's criterion.” The counterexample assumes only the category TorAb, yet step 1.1 uses [L2] to conclude that the divisible group t(D) is injective. The AC hypothesis of the cited result is not carried into the counterexample.

From “P were a nonzero projective torsion group” the proof immediately says “Choose a prime p and a nonzero map u:P→Z/pZ.” No cited result supplies this map. Nonzero torsion alone does not: Hom(Q/Z,Z/pZ)=0 for every p, since an image of the divisible group Q/Z is divisible whereas Z/pZ has no nonzero divisible subgroup. The rest of the no-projectives argument depends on this unsupported u.

The statement assumes only a split short exact sequence, while [L1] is the horseshoe theorem, whose statement requires projective resolutions of both end objects. The claim is false without them: in the abelian category of finite abelian groups, the split sequence 0→Z/pZ→Z/pZ→0→0 cannot have a projective resolution of its middle term. Any nonzero finite projective P would admit a nonzero quotient map P→Z/pZ; lifting that map through Z/p^nZ→Z/pZ for arbitrarily large n contradicts the finite order of a preimage of a nonzero element.

Step 1.1 concludes that Q and Q/Z are injective “by [L3].” The cited dependency thm-injective-modules-over-a-pid-are-exactly-divisible explicitly states “Assume the Axiom of Choice through Baer's criterion,” but neither the example statement nor its Given assumptions includes AC.

The statement assumes only a locally small abelian category with a generator. Its proof invokes [F1], “admits maximal elements by Zorn's lemma,” but thm-zorn states “Assume the Axiom of Choice.” Moreover Proof 1.1 forms the union of an arbitrary chain of partial extensions as a morphism; this requires the AB5 filtered-colimit exactness absent from the stated hypotheses. The on-disk definition def-grothendieck-category supplies precisely “an abelian category that satisfies AB5 and has a generator.”

After obtaining a pullback enlargement, the proof says “By the hypothesis on I, the induced map from that quotient extends across U, hence lifts to a map A'→I extending u_max.” No morphism from A'/A_max to I has been constructed: u_max has domain A_max, not the quotient. The hypothesis applies only to a map from a subobject of U, so it cannot yield the asserted extension of u_max across A' as written.

The lemma includes n=0, but its displayed calculation uses f_{n-1} and d_n^P as ordinary chain differentials: for n=0 this contains the undefined f_{-1}. The degree-zero case instead needs the augmentation identity ε_Q f_0=u ε_P to show that f_0d_1^P lands in ker(ε_Q).

Step 2.1 says that successive applications of the one-degree extension lemma “By induction” produce f_n in every degree. Each allowed f_{n+1} depends on the previously selected partial comparison map, so finite induction does not select the required infinite family. The on-disk definition def-dependent-choice states that exactly such “pick x_{n+1} depending on x_n, for every n at once” is not licensed without DC. The theorem states no DC (or stronger) hypothesis.

The repeated choices of h_n depend on h_0,...,h_{n-1}; the one-degree lemma supplies only a successor, while the proof asserts an entire homotopy “in every degree.” Per def-dependent-choice, this is a dependent infinite selection and requires DC. No such hypothesis is in the statement or Given assumptions.

The proof says to apply the inductive horseshoe step “repeatedly” to obtain an infinite augmented complex. Each new horseshoe lift and kernel sequence depends on the preceding one, so this is a dependent sequence of choices. The on-disk definition def-dependent-choice expressly identifies this pattern as requiring DC; no choice principle appears in the theorem's statement.

A comparison map between the two middle resolutions lifting the middle-object morphism need not commute with the fixed inclusion and projection maps of the two horseshoe short exact sequences. The proof supplies no compatible side comparison maps and no relative lifting construction, yet concludes: “Together with the side maps, this forms a morphism of short exact sequences of complexes.” The cited def-morphism-of-short-exact-sequences-of-complexes only defines such a ladder; it does not establish its required commutative squares.
